claims.text: The exceptional mechanical and thermoelastic behavior of RHEAs is driven by heterogeneous lattice strain.
Enhanced lattice distortion promotes edge-dislocation activity featuring multiple kinks and jogs under high-temperature conditions.
The altered dislocation activity maintains high-temperature strength.
The altered dislocation activity controls thermal expansion.
TiZrHfNbMo0.1 is a single-phase BCC RHEA with high configurational entropy and measurable lattice distortion.
Systematic composition changes can modulate the degree of lattice distortion.
The proposed behavior is operative from approximately 800°C to 1500°C under mechanical loading and thermal cycling.
Multi-element mixing produces heterogeneous lattice-strain fields.
Increased lattice distortion creates nonuniform internal stress fields.
Heterogeneous lattice strain changes dislocation behavior and produces multiple kinks, jogs, and cross-slip behavior.
Lattice distortion specifically favors edge dislocations over screw dislocations.
Greater lattice distortion limits plastic-zone expansion.
Limiting plastic-zone expansion helps preserve strength at high temperature.
RHEAs with greater lattice distortion will have greater high-temperature strength than lower-distortion baselines.
RHEAs with greater lattice distortion will develop smaller plastic-deformation zones than lower-distortion baselines.
RHEAs with greater lattice distortion will have more stable thermoelastic coefficients than lower-distortion baselines.
Improved performance will correlate with a dislocation network rich in edge-dislocation kinks and jogs.
Conventional refractory alloys or lower-entropy HEAs have more uniform lattices and predominantly classical screw-dislocation mechanisms under equivalent conditions.
The mechanism is restricted to single-phase BCC RHEAs at high temperature and may not apply to multiphase systems or room-temperature deformation.

Failure to observe significantly greater strength retention, reduced plastic-zone development, and prevalent edge-dislocation features in the high-distortion samples under identical conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
